tools.name: noop
tools.description: Verifies the connection end to end. Returns the caller identity, the channel it arrived on, and the server time. It is for someone checking that an API key or an MCP setup works, and it does nothing else: never call it as a step in doing what the user asked.

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Returns the signed-in user, the active workspace, the plan and the credit balance. Call this first to confirm which workspace you are acting on.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Returns the credit balance for the workspace. Credits pay for generated images, video, transcription and scraping; writing, publishing and scheduling are free on paid plans.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Returns a Stripe checkout link for a credit pack. Nothing is charged until the user opens the link and pays; the credits are added to their account as soon as Stripe confirms the payment. Packs: starter (50 credits, $4.99), growth (200, $14.99), power (500, $29.99), power_plus (1000, $49.99). Credit

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Permanently deletes the current project and everything in it: posts, scheduled posts, connected accounts, knowledge, workflows, campaigns and its API keys. Credits are not affected. Only the owner can do it, it cannot be the only project, and confirmName must be the project name exactly as the user

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Lists the social accounts connected to this workspace, with their platform, handle and whether they are currently usable. Call this before writing or scheduling, so you only offer platforms that are actually connected.

tools.name: list_subaccounts
tools.description: Lists the pages, organizations or boards an account can publish to. Facebook posts go to a page and LinkedIn can post as a company, so this is where the id for those comes from.

tools.name: choose_facebook_page
tools.description: Sets which Facebook page this project posts to, when its Facebook connection holds several. The other pages are removed from this project only. Ask the user which page belongs to this project; list_subaccounts gives the choices.

tools.name: connect_account
tools.description: Produces a link the user opens to connect a social account. Authorization happens on the platform, so give them the link and wait; the account appears in list_accounts once they have finished. Use this when an account they want is missing, or when one is marked as needing a reconnect.

tools.name: disconnect_account
tools.description: Removes a connected account and cancels anything still scheduled to it. Say how many posts that is before asking the user to confirm.

tools.name: list_instagram_accounts
tools.description: Lists the Instagram business accounts linked to the connected Facebook pages, the ones this project can post to. Facebook must be connected first. Follow with connect_instagram.

tools.name: connect_instagram
tools.description: Connects an Instagram business account found by list_instagram_accounts. With only one available, instagramId can be left out. Replaces a different Instagram account already on this project, as every connection does.

tools.name: get_tiktok_settings
tools.description: Reads, from TikTok, what the connected TikTok account may post: the account name, the privacy levels it offers, whether comments, Duet and Stitch are allowed, and the longest video. Call it before publishing to TikTok, show the user the account name, and ask them to choose the privacy level (there i

tools.name: get_youtube_settings
tools.description: Reads, from YouTube, the connected channel a Short would go to: its name and handle, who can be chosen to watch (public, unlisted, private) and the longest Short (3 minutes). Call it before publishing to YouTube, show the user the channel, and ask them for a title (at most 100 characters), who can w

tools.name: get_brand_kit
tools.description: The workspace's voice, audience, rules and example posts, which everything written for it follows. Your instructions already carry the voice and the rules (in the app and over MCP alike), so call this for the full kit: when the user asks what is set, when you are about to change something, or when y

tools.name: update_brand_kit
tools.description: Records what the workspace sounds like. Pass only the fields you are changing; anything you leave out is kept. Example posts matter most: ask for two or three things they actually published, since those define the voice better than adjectives do. Use this whenever the user tells you something about

tools.name: learn_voice_from_published
tools.description: Fills the brand kit's example posts from what this workspace has already published. Use it when the brand kit has no examples and there is a publishing history, instead of asking the user to paste posts they have already sent.

tools.name: analyze_website
tools.description: Reads the project's website and fills in what it does, who it is for, its keywords and its voice. Use it when the brand kit is empty and you know the address, instead of interviewing the user about things their own site already says. It fills only empty fields unless you say otherwise.

tools.name: list_image_models
tools.description: The image models available, what each costs in credits, and which one this workspace uses by default. Call it when the user asks what you can make images with, or before generating if they might care about the price.

tools.name: estimate_image_cost
tools.description: Says what generating would cost in credits, without generating. Use it when the user asks what something would cost. You do not need it before generating: the confirmation prompt already states the price.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Makes a picture from a description and stores it, ready to attach to a post. Call it as soon as you know what the picture should be: the user is asked to confirm the spend before it runs, with the price, so you do not need to ask them first. Describe the subject and the setting in the prompt; the mo

tools.name: set_default_image_model
tools.description: Sets which model this workspace generates with unless told otherwise. Use it when the user says they want a particular one from now on.

tools.name: list_video_models
tools.description: The video models available, what each costs per second at each resolution, and how long a clip can be. Call it when the user asks whether you can make video.

tools.name: estimate_video_cost
tools.description: Says what a video of a given length and resolution would cost in credits, without making one. Use it whenever the user has not agreed to a price, since video is the most expensive thing here.

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Makes a short video with its own audio and stores it, ready to attach to a post. It takes a few minutes: over MCP or the API it may answer with status "processing" and a jobId instead of a mediaId; then call get_video_status with that jobId until it gives the mediaId, and only then save the draft. S

tools.name: get_video_status
tools.description: Whether a video generate_video started is ready. Pass the jobId it returned. When it is done this gives the mediaId to attach to a post with save_draft, edit_post or create_post. If it is still being made, wait about a minute and ask again; never generate it a second time and never make up a media i

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Searches what this workspace has stored: notes, pages, documents, product details. Use it before writing anything factual about them, rather than guessing or asking. It searches by meaning, so ask in whatever words the user used. Returns nothing when the workspace has stored nothing, which is worth

tools.name: add_knowledge
tools.description: Stores text the workspace will want again: product details, positioning, a policy, notes from a call. Use it when the user tells you something factual worth keeping, rather than only using it in this conversation. Give it a title so it can be recognised later.

tools.name: add_knowledge_from_url
tools.description: Fetches a web page or a PDF at a URL and stores its text so it can be searched later. Use it for the workspace's own site, a product page, a press release. It reads the page as it is served, so a page that needs a sign-in will not work.

tools.name: add_knowledge_from_file
tools.description: Reads an already uploaded PDF, image or text file and stores what it says so it can be searched. Give it a media id from an upload.

tools.name: list_knowledge
tools.description: Lists what this workspace has stored, with whether each item is searchable yet. Use it when the user asks what you know about them, or when a search came back empty and you want to say why.

tools.name: delete_knowledge
tools.description: Removes a stored item and everything derived from it. Name what you are about to delete first.

tools.name: create_presigned_upload_url
tools.description: Returns a presigned URL for uploading a local file directly to storage. PUT the file bytes to uploadUrl with the same Content-Type, call complete_upload with the mediaId, then use mediaId or publicUrl when creating a post.

tools.name: complete_upload
tools.description: Call after PUTting a file to the presigned uploadUrl: checks the file arrived and records its size and type. Says so if the file is not there yet.

tools.name: upload_media_from_url
tools.description: Downloads a publicly reachable file into storage and returns a stable URL to use in posts. Use this for images or video that already live on the web.

tools.name: get_media
tools.description: Returns the stored details of one media asset, including whether its bytes have arrived.

tools.name: update_media
tools.description: Sets or clears the alt text of a picture in this project: what it shows, for people who cannot see it. Pass null or "" to clear it. At most 1000 characters. It goes out with the picture to LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram whenever a post does not give its own.

tools.name: create_post
tools.description: Publishes a post, or schedules one to be published. This is not how a draft is saved: use save_draft for that, which needs no confirmation. Publishes immediately by default; pass scheduledTime for a specific moment, or useNextFreeSlot to take the next opening in the calendar. Use variants to word th

tools.name: save_draft
tools.description: Saves a post you have written so it appears under Drafts and can be published or scheduled later. Use it whenever you write a post the user has not asked you to publish yet, instead of leaving it in the conversation: a draft in the chat is lost, a saved one is not. Always name the platforms it is fo

tools.name: edit_post
tools.description: Changes a post that already exists: its words, its pictures, the platforms it is for, or any combination. Pass only what changes; everything else stays. This is how you rewrite a draft or swap its image - do not write a second copy. Read it with get_post first when you are changing the words, since

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description: Deletes a draft, or cancels one that has not gone out yet. A post that is already published cannot be deleted here: it exists on the platform, and removing our record would not remove it.

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: The full text of one post, with its pictures, its per-platform wording and its state. Call it before changing or rewriting a post: list_posts only shows the first line of each, and working from that means working from a fragment.

tools.name: get_post_status
tools.description: Returns where a post stands on each platform, including the public link once it is live. Instagram, TikTok and YouTube process uploads in the background, so a post can be accepted and not yet visible.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description: Lists posts in this workspace, newest first, with the first line of each. Use it before writing to check what has already been said. The text here is shortened: to work on a post, read it with get_post first.

tools.name: list_top_posts
tools.description: Ranks published posts by how they did: views, likes, comments, shares, reach, saves, or engagement (likes + comments + shares + saves). Each network a post went to is ranked on its own. Numbers are the ones already collected (an hour, a day and a week after publishing, then daily for a month); nothi

tools.name: get_post_analytics
tools.description: The numbers for one published post on every network it went to: the latest reading and every earlier one, so you can say whether it is still growing. Pass refresh: true to read the networks again now (at most every ten minutes); leave it off to use what was already collected.

tools.name: list_slots
tools.description: Lists the recurring weekly openings this workspace publishes in, and which of the coming ones are already taken. Read this before scheduling, so posts land in the rhythm the user already chose.

tools.name: create_slots
tools.description: Adds recurring weekly openings to the calendar. Times are in the workspace timezone. Adding more slots than there is content for produces gaps, so ask how often the user actually wants to post.

tools.name: delete_slot
tools.description: Removes one recurring opening. Posts already scheduled into it keep their time.

tools.name: next_available_slot
tools.description: Returns the next free opening in the calendar, without taking it. Use it to tell the user when a post would go out before scheduling it.

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: Lists posts waiting to go out, soonest first.

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Changes when a post goes out, or takes it off the calendar and leaves it as a draft. Pass scheduledTime for a specific moment or useNextFreeSlot to take the next opening. A post that has already gone out cannot be moved.

tools.name: delete_schedule
tools.description: Cancels a post that has not gone out yet. A post that is already published cannot be cancelled: the platform has it and we do not.

tools.name: list_scrapers
tools.description: The networks this server can read posts from, and what each costs per result. Call it when the user asks whether you can look at a competitor.

tools.name: estimate_scrape_cost
tools.description: Says what reading someone’s posts would cost in credits, without reading anything.

tools.name: scrape_posts
tools.description: Reads recent posts from a public profile on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok or X, and keeps them so patterns across weeks can be seen. Use it to look at a competitor before writing, or as the first step of a workflow. It costs credits per post read, so say what it will cost first.

tools.name: estimate_source_cost
tools.description: Says what youtube, tiktok, audio or research would cost in credits, without reading anything. Article, PDF and plain text pages are free: use add_knowledge_from_url or add_knowledge for those instead.

tools.name: read_source
tools.description: Turns a YouTube video, a TikTok, an audio file, or a research question into text to write from. sourceType youtube or tiktok take a video url and read its spoken transcript (English captions for YouTube; TikTok's own captions when it has them, speech-to-text otherwise). sourceType audio takes a url

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: The workflows in this project, what they do, when they next run, and how the last run went. Call it when the user asks what is running on its own.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: One workflow in full: every step with its settings, its schedule, and how the last runs went. Read it before changing anything, since update_workflow replaces the steps you pass and you cannot keep what you have not seen.

tools.name: create_workflow
tools.description: Sets up work that repeats on its own: read a source, write a post, make a picture, publish it. Steps run in the order given. It is created paused and does nothing until start_workflow turns it on, so making one is safe. Use it when the user asks for something to happen daily, weekly or at a set time

tools.name: update_workflow
tools.description: Changes a workflow that already exists: its steps, its name, or when it runs. Pass only what changes. Call get_workflow first when you are changing the steps, since the list you pass replaces the ones that are there. Its run history is kept.

tools.name: start_workflow
tools.description: Turns a workflow on. From then on it runs to its schedule and publishes without asking again, so make sure the user has seen what it does. Use stop_workflow to pause it.

tools.name: stop_workflow
tools.description: Pauses a workflow so it stops running on its own. Nothing is deleted and it can be started again.

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.description: Removes a workflow and its run history. Posts it already published are untouched.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Runs a workflow immediately, whatever its schedule says, and reports what each step did. Use it to show the user what their workflow actually produces before leaving it to run on its own.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: The campaigns in this project, what each is for, and how far through it is.

tools.name: get_campaign
tools.description: One campaign in full: every planned post with its date, kind (educational, promotional, engagement, proof, behind_the_scenes, news), theme and angle, and which of them have been written. Read it before changing anything about the campaign.

tools.name: plan_campaign
tools.description: Plans a run of posts around one goal: what each post is for, its theme and its angle, spread over the days the project posts on. It writes nothing and publishes nothing - the plan is one line per post, to be read and changed before anything is written. Use this when the user wants a month of content

tools.name: update_campaign
tools.description: Changes how a campaign runs: whether its posts get a generated picture, whether it uses the calendar slots, how many days ahead it writes, or its name. Pass only what changes. Pictures apply to the posts not yet written and cost a credit each at the cheapest model - say the number before turning the

tools.name: edit_campaign_plan
tools.description: Adds posts to a campaign plan, removes planned ones, or rewrites their theme and angle. This is how you add "one more post about X" without planning the campaign again. Posts already written keep their words - use edit_post for those - and removing one that is already written is refused.

tools.name: start_campaign
tools.description: Turns a campaign on. Its posts are written a couple of days before each one goes out and land in the calendar as scheduled, where they can still be read, edited or cancelled. Posts with pictures spend credits as they are written. Tell the user how many posts and roughly how many credits before calli

tools.name: pause_campaign
tools.description: Stops a campaign writing any more posts. Posts already written keep their place in the calendar; cancel them individually if they should not go out.

tools.name: cancel_campaign_posts
tools.description: Pauses a campaign and cancels every post of it that has not gone out yet. Posts already published are untouched: they exist on the platform.

tools.name: write_campaign_posts
tools.description: Writes the next few posts of a campaign immediately instead of waiting for their lead time, and schedules them at their planned dates. Use it to show the user what the plan actually produces.

tools.name: delete_campaign
tools.description: Removes a campaign and its plan. Posts it already produced are kept - they are posts like any other, and some may be published.

tools.name: check_projects
tools.description: Counts what each of your projects holds and checks that nothing crosses between them: posts, accounts, pages, campaigns, workflows, knowledge and media. Run it after adding a project, or whenever something looks like it belongs somewhere else.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "delete_project" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Permanently deletes the current project and everything in it: posts, scheduled posts, connected accounts, knowledge, workflows, campaigns and its API keys. Cred…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_post_status" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Returns where a post stands on each platform, including the public link once it is live. Instagram and TikTok process uploads in the background, so a post can be accepted and not yet visible." → after: "Returns where a post stands on each platform, including the public link once it is live. Instagram, TikTok and YouTube process uploads in the background, so a post can be accepted and not yet visible."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
